data.title: Middle East Eye: Israel's UN ambassador rejects Vance's claim that Iran war was behind midterm losses
data.author: Bilge Kotan
data.summary:
Israel's UN ambassador rejects Vance's claim that Iran war was behind midterm losses
Israel’s ambassador to the United Nations has rejected US Vice President JD Vance’s analysis that the war on Iran was the “real reason” the Republicans suffered sweeping losses in the midterm elections, and that the party should “change our relationship to Israel”.
“It’s very easy to always blame Israel for everything, but that is not the case,” Danny Danon told Israeli outlet i24 News.
“I think it’s unfortunate that many made the link between rising prices, mainly oil prices, and the situation here in Israel,” the Israeli ambassador said.
“The decision to attack Iran was the decision of the United States. It wasn’t our decision. We supported the US effort, and we think it was the right decision.”

data.title: Middle East Eye: Israeli settlers move into homes near West Bank city
data.author: Bilge Kotan
data.summary:
Israeli settlers move into homes near West Bank city
Israeli settlers moved into houses they say they purchased near the occupied West Bank city of Jericho this week, while Palestinian officials say the sale documents were forged.
An AFP reporter saw families with children moving into homes on the outskirts of the ancient city in the West Bank.
Palestinians fear that the new settlement outpost could bring an increased army presence and settler violence.
Several Palestinian communities in the greater Jericho area have already been driven from their homes by harassment from settlers over the past year.
The Israeli families moved into eight houses just outside Jericho's city limits on Wednesday, Hanan Greenwood, a settler representative, told AFP, near the ancient site known as the Hasmonean Palaces.
Hussein Hamayel, governor of the Jericho region, told AFP that the land in question is owned by the Palestinian Authority and cannot be sold.
"What is being promoted is a forgery, not a sale, and what is being circulated is settler propaganda," Hamayel said.

data.author: Bilge Kotan
data.summary:
Israeli fire kills five in Gaza, including child
Israeli strikes and gunfire on Thursday killed five people across Gaza, including a woman and a 12-year-old boy, AFP reported, citing rescue services in the strip.
Mahmoud Bassal, spokesman for Gaza's civil defence agency, said that a 12-year-old boy was killed by Israeli gunfire east of the Al-Bureij refugee camp in central Gaza.
A few kilometres away, near the town of Al-Zawayda, two people were killed in separate Israeli strikes, he added.
The nearby Al-Aqsa Martyrs Hospital confirmed to AFP that all three were dead on arrival.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Palestine Action ban appeal enters closed proceedings at UK Supreme Court
data.author: Bilge Kotan
data.summary:
Palestine Action ban appeal enters closed proceedings at UK Supreme Court
The appeal against the ban on Palestine Action entered closed proceedings at the UK Supreme Court on Thursday, after the government and lawyers representing the group's co-founder concluded their public arguments, paving the way for judges to hear secret evidence presented by the government.
Opening the proceedings, James Eadie KC, representing the Home Office, disputed claims that Palestine Action "stood within the long tradition of civil disobedience in Britain".
"Their activities are planned and undertaken secretly in order to avoid detection," Eadie said, adding that they caused "serious damage to property".
Reiterating that the court should defer to parliament's decision to ban Palestine Action, Eadie argued that the direct-action group's track record of property damage to Israeli weapons met the legal definition of terrorism.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Aipac spent $55m on losing congressional candidates in midterm elections: Report
data.author: Bilge Kotan
data.summary:
Aipac spent $55m on losing congressional candidates in midterm elections: Report
The American Israel Public Affairs Committee (Aipac) spent more than $84m in the 2026 US midterms, but nearly two-thirds of those funds were spent on losing candidates, according to a new report from Responsible Statecraft.
Aipac’s Super Pac and other groups spent $55m on failed candidates. The largest portion of those funds, about $32m, was spent trying to defeat Democratic Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan.
The results marked one of Aipac’s worst performances in years, suggesting that the US-Israeli war on Iran, which has contributed to soaring cost-of-living issues, resonated strongly with voters.
In the 2022 midterms, Aipac’s Super Pac, United Democracy Project, saw 69 percent of its expenditure spent on races backed by the organisation that won. That number was even higher in 2024, after Israel’s genocide in Gaza, with 87 percent of its spending going to successful races.

data.author: Bilge Kotan

Turkey's parliament ratifies Mecca defence pact, clearing way for military support to Saudi Arabia
Turkey's parliament on Thursday ratified the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement, a defence pact between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkey, clearing the way for Ankara to send military support to Riyadh amid attacks by Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis against the kingdom.
Under the agreement, signed by the three regional powers in August and sent to parliament for approval last month, an attack on one party constitutes an attack on all.
A ruling party lawmaker told Reuters last month that Turkey would also submit a mandate to parliament allowing military personnel to be deployed to Saudi Arabia under the pact.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Supermajority of Jewish Americans think Israel and Aipac drive antisemitism
data.author: Bilge Kotan
data.summary:
Supermajority of Jewish Americans think Israel and Aipac drive antisemitism
A supermajority of Jewish Americans think Israel and the American Israel Public Affairs Committee’s (Aipac) actions are increasing antisemitism in the US, according to a new poll.
The poll commissioned by J Street, a US-based pro-Israel think tank, shows a deep gap between how Jewish American voters view organisations like Aipac and Israel’s occupation of the West Bank and Gaza Strip, compared to how the state of Israel and its allies in the US portray antisemitism.
The poll says 66 percent of Jewish voters in the US believe that Aipac’s campaign spending against candidates who criticise Israel actually increases antisemitism in the country.
In addition, 60 percent believe that Jewish organisations that label harsh criticism of Israel as antisemitic are exploiting concerns about antisemitism to defend unpopular Israeli government policies.
